findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (P)

Observed two large containers of cheese in stainless steel refrigerator at 133 degrees. According to kitchen staff, the food had been in there for 1.5 hours. Method of cooling is inadequate, food is not cooling quickly. This is a repeat violation. Discussed with PIC Ann and kitchen staff. Food must be rapidly cooled from 135 to 70 in first two hours, then 70-41 in the following 4 hours, equaling a 6 hour total cooling process.

Approved cooling methods include: breaking down food into shallow containers, rapidly cooling via an ice bath, or using an ice wand or ice as an ingredient in the food item (if possible, such as soups). Multiple methods may be used simultaneously as well. 
Foods in an active cooling process also may be uncovered to allow heat to escape properly, as long as the food is stored in a way it won't be contaminated by something else. 

Corrective action: food removed from cooler and placed back on stove for a rapid reheat to 165. After heating, both containers of cheese were placed into a deep ice bath. Inspector checked temperature at 15 minute mark, food observed at 135 degrees. At the 30 minute mark, food observed at 110 degrees. At the 45 minute mark, food observed at 90 degrees. After the 1 hour mark, food was placed in the walk-in cooler to continue cooling. Conduct periodic checks of cheese to ensure proper cooling time and temperatures are met.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations. There is leaking plumbing in the basement. This plumbing is not located near food, utensil, equipment or single service storage. This is indicative of a waste water leak which must be repaired as soon as possible.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-130f  Containers of salt and sugar are not marked with common name. Label containers - especially of white powders and clear liquids. Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-120(a) There was observed eggs at 80+F next to the grill. Refrigerated during the inspection. The cook stated that he hadn't used the eggs in some time & that he believed they had been out for around an hr. To insure that temperature is not abused, during non-busy times remove fewer eggs to store by the grill. A whole flat may be removed during busier periods. Choc sauce stored on the counter top. Discarded. Also, several bags of cooked red potatoes are being stored in the basement walk-in. Date marked as 2/28 - seven day rule applies. Discard after 7 days. Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 140°F or above). 750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-130(d)  There were observed fridges and freezers in the waitress area and in the kitchen with raw meat stored over ice cream, cooked noodles, corn, and various other ready-to-eat foods. During the inspection, a handout on food storage was given to the head waitress and food was properly stored. All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-280 Utensils next to drive thru pie cooler are being stored in soiled water. Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 Fresh, squishy mouse droppings are observed in the white cabinet to the right of the older ice machine of the frontline. There is nothing being stored within this cabinet, so it is probably rarely opened. Throughout the entire facility (even unused equipment storage in the basement) I did not see any other evidence of pests. During the inspection, the droppings were removed and the surface was sanitized. Adams pest control comes once a month on Monday. There are traps in place, but they are not effectively located. Adams will be contacted to place more traps and insure they are maintained next to the walls and cabinet holes. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.
